newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly lower.

text.p: CME hog futures closed narrowly mixed in quiet conditions while pork bellies were mostly lower, weakened by Friday's bearish USDA Cold Storage Report.

Floor sources said, however, the current strength of cash bellies, aided by a recent light slaughter pace, helped to limit losses. USDA reported that, as of 1115 CST, cash bellies were steady to $2.00 per cwt higher.
"The cold storage is what knocked us down but the cash is strong...I think tomorrow (Tuesday) we'll trade the cash," one floor trader said.
February bellies ended off 0.625 at 78.175 cents a lb.
Other months were off 0.775 cents to up 0.200 cent.

Friday's USDA storage data put frozen belly stocks as of November 30, at 30.943 million lbs, towards the upper end of the 26.6 million to 32.2 million range in estimates in a Reuter pre-report survey of analysts.
Floor sources said the report was mildly constructive for hogs with total red meat stocks at 630 million lbs, down from 652 million a month ago and 757 million a year ago.
Hogs were mixed as warmer weather led to a pickup in hog runs and weakness in cash markets. USDA reported interior markets in Indiana, Iowa and Illinois were $1.00 lower.
